Market-state coverage also improved: official U.S. Treasury September 22 yields and the September 23 Taipei USD/TWD close are now verified; copper has a Reuters-sourced intraday value. Actual U.S.-Iran shuttle talks and Saudi pipeline restoration reduce the energy-inflation tail risk at the margin, but Hormuz physical traffic remains severely impaired. High U.S. yields remain a valuation headwind for duration-sensitive equities.

key_drivers.name: U.S.-Iran shuttle talks
key_drivers.observed: Reuters reported the first U.S.-Iran shuttle talks for months on September 23; neither side announced a change in position or a ceasefire.
key_drivers.interpretation: Diplomatic optionality improved, reducing the energy tail risk at the margin without establishing de-escalation as a durable regime.

key_drivers.name: Taiwan export-order demand anchor
key_drivers.observed: August export orders rose 71.4% y/y to a record $103.0 billion versus verifiable Reuters consensus of +63.6%.
key_drivers.interpretation: AI/HPC/cloud demand remains a strong Taiwan semiconductor/server-chain macro support.

key_drivers.name: U.S. Treasury curve verified
key_drivers.observed: Official Treasury data for September 22 show 2Y 4.71% and 10Y 4.96%, a +25 bp 10Y-2Y spread.
key_drivers.interpretation: Nominal discount rates remain high even as the curve is modestly positive.

key_risks: Hormuz physical shipping remains severely impaired: Reuters preliminary data show only three commodity-vessel transits on September 22 versus a roughly 15-vessel 10-day moving average.
No ceasefire or verified U.S.-Iran substantive agreement has been announced despite shuttle talks.
Taiwan remains a stated Chinese red line immediately ahead of the Trump-Xi summit; no U.S. arms-sales policy change is verified.
Russia-Ukraine energy-infrastructure attacks continue to pressure refined-product supply risk.
Fed tightening and U.S. 2Y/10Y yields of 4.71%/4.96% keep global discount rates elevated.
DXY and VIX remain stale in this semantic snapshot.
